Staff.title: Staff
Staff.description: Represents a staff member with their details and work schedule associations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the staff member.

name.description: The name of the staff member.

calendarId.description: Identifier of the associated Google Calendar.

colorKey.description: Color key associated with the staff member's calendar events.

Customer.title: Customer
Customer.description: Represents a customer in the customer directory.

WorkSchedule.title: WorkSchedule
WorkSchedule.description: Represents a work schedule entry, linking staff, location, and time.

id.description: Unique identifier for the work schedule entry.

startTime.description: The start time of the work schedule.

endTime.description: The end time of the work schedule.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Represents a work location with address and geographical coordinates.

address.description: The address of the work location.

latitude.description: The latitude of the work location.

longitude.description: The longitude of the work location.

EmployeeAction.title: EmployeeAction
EmployeeAction.description: Represents an action performed by an employee during the workday (e.g., arrive, begin task).

id.description: Unique identifier for the employee action.

actionType.description: The type of action performed (e.g., arrive, begin task, finish task, depart).

timestamp.description: The timestamp of when the action was performed.

locationId.description: Reference to Location, the location at which the action was performed.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to provide a secure, scalable, and easily maintainable data model for the WorkWise application. The structure emphasizes authorization independence by denormalizing relevant authorization data (such as staff IDs in WorkSchedules and EmployeeActions). This avoids the need for `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations and simplifying debugging. Segregation of data with different access needs is achieved by using dedicated collections for each entity (Staff, Customers, Locations, WorkSchedules, and EmployeeActions). Path-based ownership is used to relate Staff to WorkSchedules and EmployeeActions. This structure allows for efficient and secure `list` operations, fulfilling the QAPs. The design incorporates explicit state modeling using status fields (if applicable in future expansions) and enforces consistent naming conventions for clarity and predictability.
